body: As Bali transforms in the face of rapid tourism development, traditional institutions that have historically supported Balinese culture must adapt. Without innovative support, such as private and corporate patronage, the island risks losing its profound aesthetic values and cultural identity.

In response to this challenge, the Tandjung Sari Foundation was established in 1987 by the visionary Wawo-Runtu family, owners of the Tandjung Sari Hotel. The foundation is dedicated to the preservation and evolution of Balinese artistic works of exceptional quality.
intro.caption: Renowned for its resilience against colonial forces, the island embodies a paradise that fiercely preserves its unique identity within Indonesia.
intro.heading: Bali stands as a beacon of rich cultural and artistic heritage, shaped by its vibrant population and noble traditions.
intro.statement: Yet, a reputation—regardless of its accuracy—cannot alone uphold a culture; a strong foundation of support is essential.

entries.description: By restoring the Banjar Sindhu gamelan group and providing traditional instruments for the rare Gamelan Semar Pegulingan, the foundation is reigniting a powerful musical legacy.

Esteemed artists inspired over one hundred local children and trainee teachers, imparting time-honored standards of excellence. They taught a range of traditional works, ensuring that these vital expressions are not lost to time.

As teachers shared their wisdom, they contributed to an “oral and visual history,” recording their knowledge of music, instruments, dance, and the intricate arts of costuming and palm leaf decoration.
The foundation also sponsors student performances, reintroducing these artistic standards to the community.

programs.heading: The foundation’s initial programs have breathed new life into the performing arts, revitalizing local banjar activities —
programs.statement: the heart of community life, where children learn to dance and where the soulful sounds of gamelan resonate.
